question: Can independent APPLAUSE scan remeasurement establish J0754 was fainter than normal in 1935-1937?
prediction: At the proper-motion-corrected catalog position, target photographic signal is weaker than predicted by same-image colour/magnitude-matched stars; a calibrated faint upper limit can support dimming even without a secure target detection.
weakening_outcomes: Comparable stars show the same deficit
Astrometric offset, blend, scratch or scan issue explains the apparent deficit
Calibration controls cannot recover withheld normal stars
Target lies outside empirically validated brightness range
Normal brightness cannot be rejected from calibrated upper limits
reason: All three independently exposed event plates in the retained target extract; 1919 reference plates from the same Lippert Astrograph with one exposure and prior target measurements. Other baseline material can be inspected later but must be labelled exploratory.
independence: Different scans/processes of one physical plate are correlated; retain them as reproducibility checks and never count them as separate epochs.
measurement: Measure raw scanned image density relative to local sky. Photographic density is nonlinear in incident flux: calibrate empirical signal versus same-image catalogue synthetic natural magnitude, never assume scanned counts are linear photon flux.
controls: Use all isolated same-image catalogue stars within available cutout, within 0.3 BP-RP of target, nearest neighbour at least 20 arcsec and clean artifact/astrometry checks; select without using target outcome. Broader colour sensitivity must be explicitly secondary.
validation: Assess held-out comparison-star predictions and empirically measured false positives at blank locations. Do not claim injection recovery of incident flux from adding a linear PSF to photographic density.
decision: Independent corroboration requires at least two physical event plates with usable calibration and either a target estimate demonstrably fainter than normal or a validated brightness upper limit excluding normal, with controls and position tests passing. Otherwise report inconclusive or a narrower result.
limits: Earlier DASCH reduction and APPLAUSE catalogue depth gates remain preserved. Pixel analysis is a separate followup with its own calibration and cannot retroactively turn below-limit catalogue values into reliable measurements.
